newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle set new highs on cash cattle gains.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle set new highs on cash cattle gains.

text.p: CME live cattle futures posted new contract highs again late as further strength in cash cattle and beef prices sparked continued short covering and fund buying that in turn, touched off buy stops, traders said.

February live cattle posted new contract highs of 67.675 cents per lb and April, 68.800 cents. Futures overall closed 0.925 to 0.325 cent higher, with April pacing the gain to settle at 68.700 cents. Feeder cattle followed to end 0.750 to 0.200 cent a lb higher with March up 0.700 at 68.200 cents.
Packers upped prices by $1 per cwt higher to $66 for cash cattle and expectations are for further gains in the near term, traders said.
"I think the driving force (in cattle prices) is we have seen the peak in marketings for the winter," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst with Brock Associates Inc.
Harper and other analysts look for cash cattle prices to rise to between $69 and $71 per cwt this spring.

Fund buying in April futures added to gains in that month. Cargill Investor Services, R.J. O'Brien and FIMAT Futures USA bought April early with Dean Witter, FIMAT and R.J. O'Brien buying late, traders said. Rosenthal Collins actively spread long August/short April, sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses actively bought April 64 puts, thought to be profit taking, floor sources said. They also bought August 68 and 70 August calls. Commercial hedging was cited in June, buying 64 puts and selling 60 puts and 67 calls, sources added.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle and rallied on scattered demand despite higher corn futures. Buy stops and lack of selling interest added to the advance with locals buying April and August late to offset scattered spreading of long deferred live cattle, short feeders. RBH bought May, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.06 at $68.84 per cwt.
